Looking at the failing tests, I need to understand what's being tested:

```
tests/test_markupsafe.py::test_string_interpolation[markupsafe._native-%i-3.14-3]
tests/test_markupsafe.py::test_string_interpolation[markupsafe._speedups-%i-3.14-3]
```

The test is using `%i` format specifier with the value `3.14`, and expecting the result to be `3`.

The `%i` format specifier converts to an integer. When you do `"%i" % 3.14`, Python calls `__int__()` on the object to get an integer value.

Looking at the `_MarkupEscapeHelper` class, the `__int__` method is used during string interpolation with the `%` operator. The current implementation has `pass`, which means it returns `None` instead of an integer.

The fix is to return `int(self.obj)`, which will convert the wrapped object to an integer.

```python
def __int__(self, /) -> int:
    return int(self.obj)
```
